definition: Stanford Alpaca is an instruction-following large language model developed by researchers at Stanford University.
details: Released in March 2023, it was created by fine-tuning LLaMA 7B on 52,000 instruction-following demonstrations generated using OpenAI's text-davinci-003 model. The project attracted attention for showing that instruction-following models could be produced from existing foundation models at relatively low cost.

explainer.lead: Stanford Alpaca showed that an instruction-following model could be built cheaply from an existing foundation model rather than trained from scratch. That made low-cost instruction tuning a widely discussed template.

tiers.eli5: Instead of teaching a student everything from zero, you take a bright student who already reads well and give them 52,000 example answers to copy the style of.
tiers.practitioner: Teams use it as a reference recipe: generate demonstrations with a stronger model, fine-tune a smaller open base model on them. A pitfall is that quality is capped by the teacher model's outputs, including its errors.
tiers.paperLevel: Alpaca is LLaMA 7B fine-tuned on 52,000 instruction-following demonstrations produced by OpenAI's text-davinci-003. Its known limit is that the training signal comes entirely from a third-party model's generated data.

explainer.example: Researchers fine-tuned LLaMA 7B on 52,000 demonstrations generated by text-davinci-003 and released the result in March 2023.
